result.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
result.summary: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N agents observe distinct viewpoints, exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and collaborate to enable a listener to answer spatial queries. We then introduce a novel multi-view spatial benchmark to isolate queries that demand non-trivial multi-view integration. Through an extensive empirical study, we discover that the penalty of restricting decentralized spatial reasoning to natural language with limited budget is far smaller than suggested by prior two-agent literature. Nevertheless, we observe that substantial headroom still remains for multi-agent spatial reasoning in this setting, as evidenced by a significant gap between current centralized performance and an oracle best-of-K ceiling. Moreover, we show that reinforcement learning with credit assignment substantially bolsters the decentralized model, effectively closing the gap with the centralized baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 该文形式化 N 个代理各自观察不同视角、在受限语言消息预算下协作回答空间查询的去中心化多视图空间推理问题，构建了隔离多视图整合查询的基准，并实证检验语言预算带来的性能损失及带信用分配的强化学习对去中心化模型的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 多视图证据筛选与预算约束下的信息传递直接关联「视觉证据被保留多少、传给谁」，其信用分配训练也对应贡献分配与监督问题；但推理状态是自然语言消息而非 latent 表示，可与 latent 通信中的信息坍缩对照核查。
